programs.title: Woman at the end of the world
programs.desc:
Martyna Wojciechowska once again sets out on a fascinating journey to learn about different aspects of the lives of women living in distant corners of the world.Some of the points of the route in this edition will be India, Senegal, South Korea, South Africa, Israel and Mexico.The program participants will talk about their everyday lives and reveal intimate secrets to the traveler.Some of them will be truly moving.This season, the journalist will look at how the Orthodox Jewish community functions on a daily basis and how they celebrate the joyful holiday of Purim.He will visit a nursing home for women who were once involved in prostitution.Although this profession is legal in Mexico, women are not entitled to any benefits.The traveler will also meet teenage Karolina, who works almost 24 hours a day at a garbage dump, and in South Africa she will meet a girl who dives with sharks.These are just some of the many amazing experiences that await Martyna Wojciechowska
Martyna Wojciechowska's goal is Mexico.This is the country where most disappearances of women occur.Kidnapped or lured, they become part of one of the most profitable businesses - prostitution.The traveler visits the nursing home intended for them.Professional sex work is legal in Mexico, but women who engage in it cannot count on any pension or health benefits.At Casa Xochiquetzal, Martyna Wojciechowska talks to eighteen residents and the director of the home, who fights for them to age with dignity and to experience warmth.

programs.title: The Extraordinary States of Procopius
programs.desc: Boston is a city of great historical and scientific importance.This is where prestigious universities such as Harvard and MIT are located, as well as the headquarters of Boston Dynamics, known for creating humanoid robots.Although the city is associated with the American Revolution, it also has lesser-known stories.Marcin will meet a guide who will talk about the first settlers and explain events such as the flooding of the city by molasses in the early 20th century, the smell of which can still be felt on hot days.Marcin will also talk to Walter Robinson from the Boston Globe about the famous journalistic investigation presented in the film "Spotlight", which revealed a scandal in the local archdiocese, affecting the city and the world.In addition, the host will take viewers to Salem, a town known for its witch trials from three hundred years ago.Today, the Salem witches attract tourists and are one of the area's main attractions.

programs.title: The Extraordinary States of Procopius
programs.desc: Horror is currently one of the most profitable genres in literature and film.Novels such as "Carrie", "Salem's Salem" and "The Shining" are considered horror classics.Their author, Stephen King, sets most of his stories in the quiet corners of Maine.Marcin Prokop visits King's hometown to understand how the environment in which the writer grew up influenced his extraordinary ability to create terrifying stories.These places are characterized by beautiful nature and peace, which attracts tourists away from the hustle and bustle of the city, creating an image of an American idyll.Marcin wants to discover what in this setting could have inspired King to write and whether the town of Derry, famous for his works, really exists under a different name.
